sections.content: While CSS transitions/keyframes handle most needs, libraries like GSAP, Framer Motion, and Animate.css add timelines, scroll triggers, and physics.
Rule of thumb: CSS-first for simple hover/state changes, JS libraries only when you need sequencing, scroll-linked, or complex choreography. Over-animating hurts UX and performance.
Key points: respect prefers-reduced-motion in every animation, transform/opacity only for smooth 60fps, and exit animations need JS or view transitions.
